# Print an optspec for argparse to handle cmd's options that are independent of any subcommand.
function __fish_norn_global_optspecs
	string join \n p/print m/model= profile= S/system-prompt= append-system-prompt= allowed-tools= disallowed-tools= reasoning-effort= service-tier= fast max-turns= timeout= C/working-dir= workspace-root= c/config= rules= variables= e/extension= mcp-config= channel= channel-max-retained-messages= channel-max-retained-bytes= channel-overflow= s/output-schema= event-schema= f/output-format= protocol= o/output= q/quiet partial r/resume= fork= no-session session-name= session-id= resume-if-exists allow-degraded-session account= provider= api-shape= provider-profile= debug-api= h/help V/version
end

function __fish_norn_needs_command
	# Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
	set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
	set -e cmd[1]
	argparse -s (__fish_norn_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
	or return
	if set -q argv[1]
		# Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
		echo $argv[1]
		return 1
	end
	return 0
end

function __fish_norn_using_subcommand
	set -l cmd (__fish_norn_needs_command)
	test -z "$cmd"
	and return 1
	contains -- $cmd[1] $argv
end
